question.prompt:
Triangle \(ABC\) in the figure has area \(10.\) Points \(D,\) \(E\) and \(F,\) all distinct from \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C,\) are on sides \(AB,\) \(BC\) and \(CA\) respectively, and \(AD=2,\) \(DB=3.\) If triangle \(ABE\) and quadrilateral \(DBEF\) have equal areas, then that area is

[Figure 1](figures/1983_AMC_12_Q28_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Write \([PQR]\) for the area of triangle \(PQR\). Drawing \(DE\) splits both figures in the given area equality into triangles:
\[
[ABE]=[ADE]+[BDE],
\qquad
[DBEF]=[DEF]+[BDE].
\]
Subtracting their common part \([BDE]\) gives \([ADE]=[DEF]\).

These two triangles have the same base \(DE\), so their perpendicular heights from \(A\) and \(F\) are equal. The segment \(DE\) cuts off the corner triangle \(BDE\); both \(A\) and \(F\) lie on its other side. Points at a fixed perpendicular distance on one side of a line lie on a parallel line. Thus \(AF\parallel DE\). Since \(F\) lies on \(AC\) and \(F\ne A\), this means \(DE\parallel AC\).

Parallel segments in triangle \(BAC\) now give
\[
\frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{BD}{BA}=\frac3{2+3}=\frac35.
\]
Triangles \(ABE\) and \(ABC\) have bases \(BE\) and \(BC\) on the same line and the same height from \(A\). Their areas have the same ratio as those bases. Therefore the requested common area is
\[
[ABE]=\frac35[ABC]=\frac35\cdot10=\boxed6,
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Subtract the common triangle

solutions.explanation:
Let \(S\) be the common area of triangle \(ABE\) and quadrilateral \(DBEF\), and write \([PQR]\) for a triangle's area. Set
\[
t=\frac{AF}{AC}.
\]
Because \(F\) is strictly between \(A\) and \(C\), we have \(0<t<1\). We will partition the whole triangle into \(ADF\), \(DBEF\), and \(CEF\).

First, triangles \(ADC\) and \(ABC\) share the height from \(C\) to \(AB\), so
\[
[ADC]=\frac{AD}{AB}[ABC]=\frac25\cdot10=4.
\]
Triangles \(ADF\) and \(ADC\) have bases \(AF\) and \(AC\) on the same line and the same height from \(D\). Hence \([ADF]=4t\).

Also, \(AE\) divides \(ABC\) into \(ABE\) and \(ACE\), giving \([ACE]=10-S\). Comparing bases \(CF\) and \(CA\) with the common height from \(E\) gives
\[
[CEF]=(1-t)[ACE]=(1-t)(10-S).
\]
Adding the three pieces of \(ABC\), we obtain
\[
10=4t+S+(1-t)(10-S)=10+t(S-6).
\]
Thus \(t(S-6)=0\). Since \(t>0\), division by \(t\) is valid and yields \(S=\boxed6\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
